name: 5:2 diet / alternate-day fasting

card.summary: Two very low-calorie days a week, or every other day: weight loss comparable in scope to ordinary dieting, with limited evidence it does better.
card.note: Not recommended for pregnancy, adolescents, or people with eating disorders.

quick.overview:
The 5:2 diet restricts intake to roughly 500 to 600 calories on two non-consecutive days a week; alternate-day fasting alternates fast and normal days. Both are forms of intermittent fasting.

Studies report modest weight loss, and evidence that they beat continuous calorie restriction is limited.
quick.mechanism: Weekly calorie intake falls because of the low days; fat and some lean mass are lost, and reviews propose exercise to help retain lean mass.
quick.risks: Hunger, irritability, dizziness and headaches are common early. Health bodies say it is not recommended for pregnancy, children, older adults, underweight people or those with eating disorders.

lead: The 5:2 diet and alternate-day fasting are two forms of intermittent energy restriction used to get leaner. The 5:2 pattern has two non-consecutive low-calorie days of roughly 500 to 600 calories and normal eating on the other five; alternate-day fasting alternates a very low-calorie day (under about 25 percent of usual needs) with a normal "feast" day, and a modified version allows up to 25 percent of calories on fast days [1]. The appearance payoff people seek is lower body fat: a slimmer waist, more visible muscle definition and a sharper face.

The 5:2 pattern was documented in a 2011 article by Harvie and colleagues and was popularized in the UK and Australia by Michael Mosley through the 2012 BBC Horizon documentary Eat, Fast and Live Longer [1]. Reviews report weight loss of about 2.5 to 9.9 percent in most human studies, and a 2023 meta-analysis of 24 trials concluded that intermittent fasting produced weight loss comparable to continuous calorie restriction, ranking alternate-day fasting highest of the three regimens compared [1][4].

On looksmaxxing forums the approach is described as a way to cut without counting calories every day. One looksmax.org thread titled '5/2 fasting is the best way to get shredded' has a user reporting a drop from 340 to 271 lbs in two months [6].

chain: Two (or alternate) very low-calorie days each week
Fat loss that shows as a leaner face, waist and more visible muscle
angle.text: Fasting days lower weekly calories without requiring daily restriction, which is how people use the pattern to lose body fat. Fat loss makes the face and midsection look leaner and brings out muscle definition; adherence and lean-mass retention are the factors researchers examine [1][3].

infobox: Two non-consecutive low-calorie days (about 500-600 kcal) per week
Fast day alternating with normal-eating day

paras: Both protocols are grouped with time-restricted eating under intermittent fasting, all involving alternating periods of fasting and ad libitum eating [2]. Periodic or whole-day fasting with water only is a separate category [1].

People using these protocols for appearance typically aim to lose fat while keeping training volume. Like other diets, intermittent fasting typically induces loss of both fat and lean mass, and a 2025 narrative review proposes exercise as an adjunct to retain lean mass [2]. A 2024 randomized trial in adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes compared a 5:2 diet (two days per week of formula-diet energy restriction) with a high-intensity interval plus resistance exercise program and routine education on glycemic control and cardiometabolic health [5].

A 2025 BMJ systematic review and network meta-analysis of 99 randomized trials with 6,582 adults compared intermittent fasting (alternate-day, time-restricted and whole-day fasting), continuous energy restriction and ad libitum diets on body weight and cardiometabolic outcomes [3]. A 2020 systematic review in Canadian Family Physician covered 27 trials and found weight loss of 0.8 to 13.0 percent of baseline weight with no serious adverse events, with 12 studies comparing intermittent fasting with calorie restriction reporting equivalent results [7].

A 2023 meta-analysis of 24 trials (1,768 participants) found that intermittent fasting produced weight loss similar to continuous restriction (mean difference 0.26 kg), with compliance above 80 percent in trials shorter than 3 months [4]. A 2024 umbrella review reported improvements in waist circumference, fat mass, LDL cholesterol, triglycerides and fasting insulin, with a smaller blood-pressure benefit than continuous calorie restriction [1]. A 2021 review reported that moderate alternate-day fasting for 2 to 6 months reduced weight, BMI and cardiometabolic risk factors [1]. A 2017 JAMA Internal Medicine trial examined alternate-day fasting for weight loss, maintenance and cardioprotection in metabolically healthy obese adults [8]. A Cochrane review found it uncertain whether intermittent fasting prevents cardiovascular disease [1].

A review on women's health discusses intermittent energy restriction in women with overweight and with healthy weight, noting reduced adherence to daily restriction as a reason for developing intermittent regimens [9]. Reported dropout rates were 2 to 38 percent for intermittent fasting versus 0 to 50 percent for calorie restriction [1].

Short-term effects include hunger, irritability, dizziness, nausea, headaches and impaired thinking, which usually fade within a month [1]. It is not recommended for pregnant or breastfeeding women, children and adolescents, older adults, underweight people, or those with or at risk of eating disorders [1].

The US National Institute on Aging says research is limited and inconclusive and does not recommend these diets for the general public; the American Heart Association says there is no good evidence of heart-health benefits; the UK NHS advises people considering 5:2 to consult a physician first [1].

timeline.event: Harvie and colleagues document the 5:2 diet [1].
JAMA Internal Medicine trial of alternate-day fasting in metabolically healthy obese adults [8].
BMJ network meta-analysis of 99 randomized trials of intermittent fasting [3].

lore.intro: Fasting for fat loss comes up on looksmax.org as a way to get lean and reveal facial and abdominal definition, usually presented through personal transformation stories [6].

claims.claim: 5:2 fasting is a fast route to getting shredded
claims.believers: A looksmax.org user reported dropping from 340 to 271 lbs in two months on 5:2 and received congratulations from other members [6].
claims.experts: Trials report average weight loss of about 2.5 to 9.9 percent and generally find it comparable to continuous calorie restriction rather than better [1][4].
